Viewed through flexible inflation targeting and forecast-based policy (Svensson and Woodford, 2005; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), the FOMC’s quarter-point cut to 4.5–4.75% while continuing balance-sheet runoff indicates a cautiously constructive stance: activity is “solid,” labor conditions are easing, and inflation is progressing toward target, but remaining “somewhat elevated” and an uncertain outlook restrain exuberance. The use of IOER and ON RRP to implement a floor system (Goodfriend, 2002) underscores operational control and a still-restrictive policy setting, and the “balanced risks” language aligns with Taylor-type prescriptions that weigh deviations of both inflation and employment from goals. Overall tone: mildly positive, tempered by caution.
